A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAVS task and CMR framework. Full inspection of v1's ten pages and v2's fifteen pages, including Appendix A, supports reliable matching of text, equations, figures, tables, and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on AVSBench-CI, CIS, and CIM, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, backbone comparisons, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional PVT results for the 60-5 setting in Table 5.

M1.justification: MSS still selects samples using the smallest absolute difference between audiovisual and visual-only mIoU. CSR retains collision counting, sigmoid smoothing, and 20% memory resampling. Algorithm 1 is renamed and reformatted without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AVSBench-derived continual segmentation tasks, covering 70 sounding-object categories, single-object and multiple-object videos, and disjoint and overlapped streams. No new dataset, domain, or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table I/1 retains FT, LwF, LwF-MC, ILT, MiB, PLOP, AVSegFormer, EIR, and the offline upper bound. Figure 5's comparator membership is also unchanged. The added table extends the existing ResNet/PVT comparison.

E3.justification: Class splits, mIoU evaluation, training budgets, and memory settings remain unchanged. v1 Section IV.D already describes PVT experiments for both 60-10 and 60-5; v2's additional results do not establish a new or revised protocol.

E4.justification: v2 supplies additional backbone-analysis evidence for 60-5 in Table 5, but removes v1 Section IV.F.6 and Figure 11's violin/bassoon confusion case study. Component ablations, memory-size sensitivity, collision statistics, and other qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mIoU point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 Table 5 newly reports PVT 60-5 all-class mIoU of 35.2 for disjoint and 22.2 for overlapped settings; its ResNet values already appeared in v1 Table I. Main benchmark, retained ablation, and 60-10 backbone scores are unchanged. The violin/bassoon qualitative error example is removed.

T1.justification: v1 Equation (1)'s pixel-label argmax definition becomes an incomplete max expression in v2 Section 3.1, changing its mathematical meaning. The CAVS prediction equation, formerly Equation (2), is omitted from Section 3.2. Remaining MSS/CSR formulas are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the CAVS novelty claim, the two modality-entanglement challenges, the MSS/CSR contributions, and the state-of-the-art performance claim. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 Section 4.6 adds the qualification that stronger PVT backbones still suffer forgetting in the 60-5 overlapped setting. It removes the case-specific interpretation of accurate bassoon localization with incorrect audio-derived class alignment. The existing limitation concerning multi-target rehearsal remains.

D1.justification: v1 Section IV.B.3 explicitly states that memory data are shuffled together with training data; v2 Appendix A.3 omits this detail. Hardware, batch size, epochs, input resolution, and memory budgets are retained. The omission does not establish an actual training change.

R1.justification: v2 removes the MMH discussion and its citation to Wei et al.'s Privileged Modality Learning via Multimodal Hallucination. The remaining multimodal review, including the distinctions from Finger and Open-set AVS, is largely retained in Appendix A.1.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: multimodal related work, evaluation details, baseline descriptions, and several qualitative analyses move into Appendix A, while experimental subsections are reordered. Most prose is retained with local corrections, but v2 introduces an unfinished abstract ending and duplicate collision-analysis headings.

P2.justification: The two-column journal layout becomes a single-column preprint layout, Figure 2 is redrawn, and numerous displays are relocated or rearranged. v2 adds Table 5 and removes v1 Figure 11. The unchanged collision plot becomes Table 7, although its discussion still references Figure 7.

improvement.justification: Table 5 usefully completes the reported 60-5 PVT evidence, and Section 4.6 adds an appropriate qualification about persistent forgetting. However, v2 introduces a malformed label definition, omits the CAVS prediction equation, removes a diagnostic case study, and leaves an unfinished abstract and incorrect appendix reference. With the central method and benchmark findings unchanged, these losses in precision and completeness outweigh the limited evidential addition.
